classification.difficultyReason: Choose addition or subtraction according to whether the unknown is a whole angle or a component.

content.prompt: Find the value of the pronumeral in each diagram.

spec.description: Three arms meet at the right-hand vertex. A double-ended outer arc on the left spans both labelled sectors. Source proportions are retained without treating the drawing as a measured construction.
spec.mathematics: The 26° and 58° adjacent sectors together form c°. c = 84.
spec.answerVisibility: Only c°, 26° and 58° are visible in the question. The printed blue 84° is answer evidence.

answer.worked:
Adjacent angles add to the whole angle.
$$\begin{align*}c &= 26+58\\c &= 84\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Horizontal right arm and two nearly vertical downward arms. A left pointer identifies the narrow 5° sector. The double-ended outer arc spans both sectors. No right-angle square.
spec.answerVisibility: 85°, 5° and y° remain visible. The printed blue 90° is answer evidence.

answer.worked:
Adjacent angles add to the whole angle.
$$\begin{align*}y &= 85+5\\y &= 90\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Steep upward, upper-right and lower-right arms share a left-hand vertex. The outer right arc crosses the middle arm and spans the combined non-reflex angle.
spec.answerVisibility: 26°, 100° and p° remain visible. The printed blue 126° is answer evidence.

answer.worked:
Adjacent angles add to the whole angle.
$$\begin{align*}p &= 26+100\\p &= 126\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Horizontal straight line and a down-left arm. Both 50° and 130° remain beneath the line. The double-ended lower arc spans the straight angle and crosses the down-left arm.
spec.answerVisibility: 50°, 130° and a° remain visible. The printed blue 180° is answer evidence.

answer.worked:
Adjacent angles add to the whole angle.
$$\begin{align*}a &= 50+130\\a &= 180\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Three leftward arms meet at the right-hand vertex. x° is above the middle arm and 58° below it. The outer double-ended arc is labelled 70°. Preserve the source's unequal visual and numerical sector proportions.
spec.answerVisibility: 70°, x° and 58° remain visible. The printed blue 12° is answer evidence.

answer.worked:
Adjacent angles add to the whole angle.
$$\begin{align*}x+58 &= 70\\x &= 12\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A rightward arm and two down-left arms meet at the upper vertex. x° labels the narrow sector; 80° labels the sector adjoining the rightward arm. The outer lower arc spans both and is labelled 120°. Source appearance is retained without inferring measures from slopes.
spec.answerVisibility: x°, 80° and 120° remain visible. The printed blue 40° is answer evidence.

answer.worked:
Adjacent angles add to the whole angle.
$$\begin{align*}x+80 &= 120\\x &= 40\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Vertical and horizontal arms form a marked right angle. The intermediate upper-right arm crosses the square's region. The upper sector is a° and the lower sector is 75°. Retain the source diagonal direction, which is not numerically to scale.
spec.mathematics: The square supplies the total 90°. a + 75 = 90, so a = 15.
spec.answerVisibility: a°, 75° and the right-angle square remain visible. The printed blue 15° is answer evidence.

answer.worked:
Angles in a right angle add to $90^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a+75 &= 90\\a &= 15\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Steep upper-left, shallow upper-right and horizontal right arms share the lower-left vertex. The outer double-ended arc spans the combined non-reflex angle and crosses the middle arm. The source slopes are not numerical angle measurements.
spec.answerVisibility: 115°, a° and 161° remain visible. The printed blue 46° is answer evidence.

answer.worked:
Adjacent angles add to the whole angle.
$$\begin{align*}115+a &= 161\\a &= 46\end{align*}$$
